message.content:
Search this Go repository very thoroughly for every place where memo visibility is enforced — meaning where code checks whether the current user is allowed to view/access a memo based on its visibility setting (PUBLIC, PROTECTED, PRIVATE).

Look for:
- Direct visibility checks (comparing memo.Visibility to constants like PRIVATE, PROTECTED, PUBLIC)
- Access control functions that gate memo reading (e.g., checkMemoReadAccess, checkAccessibility, canAccessMemo)
- Any middleware or interceptor that filters memos by visibility
- SQL-level visibility filtering in queries
- RSS/feed endpoints that filter by visibility
- File server or attachment serving that checks parent memo visibility

Search terms: "visibility", "PRIVATE", "PROTECTED", "PUBLIC", "ReadAccess", "checkAccess", "Visibility_PRIVATE", "Visibility_PROTECTED", "readAccess", "memo access".

I need every DISTINCT enforcement site — the actual function/method that performs the check, with file path and line numbers. Search breadth: very thorough.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

---

## Complete Inventory of Memo Visibility Enforcement Sites

Below is every distinct enforcement site in the codebase, grouped by category. Each entry lists the file, line number(s), function, and what it does.

---

### 1. Central Access-Check Function: `checkMemoReadAccess`

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 39-68

This is the primary reusable access gate. Logic:
- Archived memos: only visible to their creator (lines 45-53).
- Non-PUBLIC memos require an authenticated user (lines 55-62).
- PRIVATE memos: only the memo creator may access (line 63-64). Note: does NOT grant admin/superuser override.

**Call sites:**
- `GetMemo` -- line 356 (on the memo itself) and line 367 (on the parent memo, if the memo is a comment).
- `ListMemoComments` -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`, line 148.

---

### 2. `ListMemos` -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 178-227

In the `ListMemos` method:
- **Anonymous user** (line 218-219): `VisibilityList` is set to `[Public]` only.
- **Authenticated, listing all creators** (lines 221-223): appends a CEL filter `creator_id == <userID> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` -- the user sees their own memos plus PUBLIC/PROTECTED.
- **Authenticated, listing another user's memos** (lines 224-225): `VisibilityList` set to `[Public, Protected]`.
- **Archived memos** (lines 188-195): only the creator's own archived memos are listed.

---

### 3. `ListMemoComments` -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`, lines 136-161

- First calls `checkMemoReadAccess` on the parent memo (line 148).
- Then applies filter-level visibility: anonymous gets `visibility == "PUBLIC"` (line 158); authenticated gets `creator_id == <userID> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` (line 160).

---

### 4. `CreateMemoComment` -- Visibility Check Before Allowing Comment

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`, lines 20-52

- Line 41: If the parent memo is PRIVATE and the user is neither its creator nor a super user, the request is denied.
- Line 52: The comment's visibility is forced to match the parent memo's visibility.
- Line 100: Inbox notification is only sent if the comment is NOT PRIVATE and the commenter is not the parent memo's creator.

---

### 5. `ListMemoReactions` -- Inline Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`, lines 15-41

- Lines 30-41: If memo is not PUBLIC, requires authentication. If PRIVATE, only the creator or a super user can list reactions.

---

### 6. `UpsertMemoReaction` -- Inline Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`, lines 60-85

- Line 83: If memo is PRIVATE and the user is neither creator nor super user, the request is denied.

---

### 7. `ListMemoAttachments` -- Inline Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`, lines 200-225

- Lines 214-224: If memo is not PUBLIC, requires authentication. If PRIVATE, only the creator or a super user can list attachments.

---

### 8. `GetAttachment` via `checkAttachmentAccess` -- Memo Visibility Delegation

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`, lines 419-455

The `checkAttachmentAccess` function (defined at line 422, called at line 256 from `GetAttachment`):
- Unlinked attachments: only the creator (or super user) can access (lines 426-433).
- Linked attachments: fetches the parent memo (line 437) and applies visibility rules:
  - PUBLIC: anyone (line 445).
  - Non-public without auth: denied (lines 448-449).
  - PRIVATE: only the creator or super user (line 451).

---

### 9. File Server: `checkAttachmentPermission` -- HTTP-Level Visibility Check

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, lines 649-703

Called at line 149 from `serveAttachmentFile`. This is the HTTP file-serving layer (separate from the gRPC API). Logic:
- Unlinked attachments: only the creator or admin (lines 652-664).
- PUBLIC memo + anonymous instance (`AllowAnonymous()`): served to anyone (line 677).
- Share token fallback: if the request carries a valid, non-expired share token for this memo, access is granted (lines 684-688).
- Otherwise, requires an authenticated user (lines 691-696).
- PRIVATE memo: only the creator or admin (line 699).

---

### 10. `ListMemoRelations` -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`, lines 93-117

- Anonymous: `memoFilter = visibility == "PUBLIC"` (line 109).
- Authenticated: `creator_id == <userID> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` (line 111).
- The filter is passed as `MemoFilter` to `Store.ListMemoRelations`, which applies it at the SQL level.

---

### 11. `batchConvertMemoRelations` -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 170-198

Used when converting memo lists (e.g., in `ListMemos`). Applies the same pattern:
- Anonymous: `visibility == "PUBLIC"` (line 184).
- Authenticated: `creator_id == <userID> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` (line 186).

---

### 12. `ListAllUserStats` -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`, lines 56-92

- Anonymous (line 84): `VisibilityList = [Public]`.
- Authenticated, listing all (lines 86-88): CEL filter `creator_id == <userID> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`.
- Authenticated, listing another user (line 90): `VisibilityList = [Public, Protected]`.

---

### 13. `GetUserStats` -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`, lines 193-221

- Anonymous (line 218): `VisibilityList = [Public]`.
- Authenticated viewing another user (lines 219-220): `VisibilityList = [Public, Protected]`.

---

### 14. RSS Feeds -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`

- `GetRSS` (global feed), line 90: `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` -- only PUBLIC memos in the global RSS feed.
- `GetUserRSS` (per-user feed), line 141: `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` -- only PUBLIC memos in a user's RSS feed.

---

### 15. Frontend/Sitemap -- Query-Level Visibility Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`, line 150

- `getSitemapXML`: `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` -- only PUBLIC memos appear in the sitemap.

---

### 16. SSE Hub: `canReceive` -- Event Delivery Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`, lines 134-144

Filters which SSE clients receive which events:
- PRIVATE events: only delivered to the creator or an admin (line 137).
- PUBLIC, PROTECTED, or empty: delivered to all clients (line 138).

---

### 17. `canViewerAccessMemo` -- Notification Visibility Gate (API layer)

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`, lines 302-316

Used when converting inbox/notification items to ensure the viewer can still see the memo:
- Super user: always true (lines 306-307).
- PRIVATE: only if viewer is the creator (lines 309-310).
- PROTECTED: only if viewer is authenticated (lines 312-313).
- PUBLIC: always true (line 315).

**Call sites in same file:**
- `convertMemoCommentNotificationPayload` -- lines 337, 342.
- `convertMemoMentionNotificationPayload` -- lines 370, 385.

---

### 18. `canViewerAccessMemo` -- Notification Visibility Gate (Email layer)

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go`, lines 306-320

Identical logic to the API-layer version (duplicated in the notification/email package):
- PRIVATE: only creator (line 313-314).
- PROTECTED: only authenticated/non-nil viewer (line 316-317).

**Call sites in same file:**
- `buildMemoCommentEmailMessage` -- line 155.
- `buildMemoMentionEmailMessage` -- line 187.

---

### 19. `canUserAccessMentionContext` -- Mention Notification Filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`, lines 56-72

Determines whether a mentioned user can see the memo context:
- If the related memo is PRIVATE and the target is not its creator, returns false (line 62).
- If the memo itself is PRIVATE and the target is not its creator, returns false (line 67).

Called by `shouldSkipMentionInbox` (line 88), which is called by `dispatchMemoMentionNotifications` (line 113).

---

### 20. `shouldSkipMentionInbox` -- Comment/Mention Inbox Suppression

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`, lines 74-89

- Line 84: Skips sending a mention inbox if the related memo exists and the target is the related memo's creator and the memo visibility is NOT PRIVATE and the commenter is different from the related memo's creator (avoids duplicate notification with the comment notification).
- Line 88: Delegates to `canUserAccessMentionContext` -- skips if the target cannot see the memo.

---

### 21. `UpdateMemo` -- Visibility Inheritance for Comments

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 452-464

When updating a memo's visibility:
- If the memo is a comment (has `ParentUID`), the visibility update is overridden to match the parent memo's visibility (lines 454-462). This prevents a comment from becoming more visible than its parent.

---

### 22. SQL-Level Enforcement: `VisibilityList` Filtering

**Files:**
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go`, lines 96-102
- `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go`, lines 89-95

When `FindMemo.VisibilityList` is populated, a SQL `WHERE memo.visibility IN (...)` clause is added to the query. This is the database-level enforcement used by all the query-level filtering above.

---

### 23. SQL-Level Enforcement: `MemoFilter` on Relations

**Files:**
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go`, line 80
- `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go`, line 82

When `FindMemoRelation.MemoFilter` is set, it is compiled via the CEL filter engine and applied as a SQL sub-clause, filtering out related memos the user should not see.

---

### 24. CEL Filter Schema: `visibility` Field

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/filter/schema.go`, lines 162-166, 241

Defines `visibility` as a filterable string field mapping to `memo.visibility` in SQL. This enables the CEL-based filter expressions used throughout the service layer (e.g., `visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`).

---

### 25. `Authorizer.CheckAccess` / `AuthInterceptor` -- Method-Level Authentication Gate

**Files:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/authz.go`, lines 58-69 (CheckAccess)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`, lines 11-41 (PublicMethods map)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`, lines 217-231 (Connect interceptor)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`, lines 69-84 (gRPC-Gateway middleware)

While not a visibility check per se, this is the outer authentication layer that determines whether anonymous callers can reach memo endpoints at all. `GetMemo`, `ListMemos`, `ListMemoComments`, and `GetMemoByShare` are in the `PublicMethods` map and reachable anonymously (on open instances), with the service layer then enforcing visibility. All other memo endpoints require authentication at this layer.

---

### 26. `GetMemoByShare` -- Share-Token Based Access (Bypasses Normal Visibility)

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go`, lines 153-192

This endpoint requires no authentication. It resolves a share token to a memo directly, bypassing the normal visibility checks. The only gates are:
- The share token must be valid and not expired (line 154, calling `getActiveMemoShare`).
- The memo must exist and not be archived (line 164).
